exposure: Maternal birthing position (upright, dorsal, planned cesarean)
outcome: Duration of second stage of labor
cohort: 750 women with term breech deliveries at a center in Frankfurt, Germany, between January 2004 and June 2011.
finding: Upright vaginal breech delivery was associated with fewer delivery maneuvers, neonatal birth injuries, and shorter second stages of labor compared to vaginal delivery in the dorsal position.
mod_finding: Upright vaginal breech delivery was associated with fewer delivery maneuvers, neonatal birth injuries, shorter second stages of labor, and a decreased cesarean rate compared to vaginal delivery in the dorsal position.
